claims.text: The transient ductile-brittle-ductile transition in FCC+B2 eutectic HEAs is driven by evolution of local chemical order within B2 and accompanying phase-boundary morphology changes.
Intermediate aging initially promotes formation of short-range local chemical orders, described as B2 ordering, within the B2 phase.
Formation of these local chemical orders increases the Peierls stress for dislocation glide in B2.
Dislocations become pinned by, or require higher stress to cut through, the ordered domains, causing the ductility loss.
Further aging or aging at higher temperatures causes local chemical orders to coarsen or transform into larger, more stable ordered domains.
Aging changes phase boundaries from coherent toward semi-coherent or incoherent morphologies.
Coarsened local order and changed phase-boundary morphology facilitate dislocation transmission or cross-slip.
Easier dislocation motion after coarsening and phase-boundary evolution restores ductility.
The proposed mechanism is intragranular and phase-boundary controlled rather than caused by impurity segregation at grain boundaries.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can contain disordered FCC and ordered B2 phases.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure can be lamellar or nanolamellar.
The relevant intermediate-aging window is 400–700 °C for 10–1000 hours.
The structural mediator includes changes in local-order degree and cluster size, as well as phase-boundary coherence, roughness, and minor-element segregation.
Ordered phases generally have higher strength and lower ductility because they impede dislocations.
Coarsening of ordered domains reduces obstacle density per unit volume and can restore ductility.
Minimum elongation will occur after approximately 100–200 hours, when local chemical orders have an optimal size for dislocation pinning.
The embrittlement regime is approximately 400–600 °C and 50–300 hours.
A conventional grain-boundary impurity-segregation mechanism would produce a monotonic ductility decrease with aging and no subsequent recovery.
During the brittle regime, in-situ deformation should show dislocations pinned or blocked at local-order clusters and phase boundaries.
The local-order cluster size should be at its minimum, or finest, at the time of peak brittleness.

contradictions.description: The initial state already identifies B2 as an ordered phase, while the mechanism describes aging as forming B2 ordering or short-range B2 order within that B2 phase. The hypothesis does not distinguish changes in degree of pre-existing long-range B2 order from formation of new local order.

Peak brittleness is attributed to an unspecified optimal LCO size, but the falsification rule requires the peak to coincide specifically with the minimum or finest cluster size. These are not necessarily equivalent.
